conclusion: At this fixed complete single-entry update episode, no obvious regression was observed. This does not establish zero sorting overhead or equal cost for every capacity/update pattern.

smoke: Both arms passed 16 warm plus 32 untimed complete episodes.
formal: Exactly old/new/new/old: each process 16 warm plus 9 epochs of 128 timed episodes. All 36 epochs preserved in order; no AA, new shape, sample rejection or rerun.
ownership: Each completed episode retains one version, no draft, 1024 blocks and two roots; each pool has 512 live blocks and 32832 B capacity. Each update retires exactly one old block, checked via both pool counters.
actual_identity: All formal processes read back LP4 mask16/current CPU4, normal priority32/thread0, QPC10MHz and minimum observed positive step1 tick/100ns. PIDs and original identity records remain.
oracle: Every episode checks all10 StoreStats fields, both pools capacity/allocated/live/max/active/reclaimed/closed/peak bounds, old/new64B payload and observable checksum. Full1024-entry payload is checked outside QPC after every epoch. All passed.
source_vs_runtime: Alternating roots can trigger ledger reordering, as discussed in the plan. No per-sort counter or profiler was added; do not claim an observed exact sort frequency or attribute the timing delta only to sort.
limits: Whole episode includes pool allocation/fill/publish, begin/finalize reference copies, replacement/preflight/retain, old owner drop, collect, stats and identical checks. Initial interleaved import and destruction are excluded. No capacity matrix, clone-route or pure-sort timing claim.
original_evidence: Original v1/v2 archives and144 hot epochs are untouched. plan.json preserves the pre-execution proposal; commands.json and this summary record actual execution.
